why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Checks 1 and 2 test only what their lines say: clamp is exported, it returns x limited to the range (lo equal to hi is still a range), and it throws a RangeError when lo is greater than hi. Check 3 breaks the criterion. It FAILs any exported function whose name is not followed by "(" in README.md (`!md.includes(n+"(")`). That is an exact-wording rule. "README.md documents every function" does not force it, because a README could describe `clamp` without writing "clamp(". This rule should have been under Advisory. Check 4 is also somewhat stricter than "npm test passes", since it also requires the TAP output to show "# fail 0" on top of exit 0. Because check 3 fails, the criterion does not hold for the whole output.
